CHIEF COMPLAINT
Shortness of breath.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Rachel is a 48-year-old female presenting with shortness of breath and palpitations. She reports these symptoms occur during mild exercise or walking, such as walking up her driveway. She is unsure if the shortness of breath is related to her chronic back pain. She notes these episodes are happening more frequently lately. She reports recently increasing her exercise routine to lose weight. She previously smoked 2 packs per day but has significantly reduced to approximately 1 cigarette per day.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies any other issues.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, smoking history, chronic back pain.

MEDICATIONS
Effexor for depression, Gabapentin (Neurontin) for chronic back pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Current smoker, reduced from 2 packs per day to approximately 1 cigarette per day. Recently increased exercise to address weight gain from COVID-19. Discussed doing yoga but has not made it a habit.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Physical exam appears mostly normal. Mild wheezes noted in all lung fields.

RESULTS
Pulmonary function tests show possible asthma or COPD. Chest X-ray shows flattened diaphragm consistent with COPD, commonly seen in smokers.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) diagnosed. Patient started on Combivent 2 puffs twice daily to help open lungs. Albuterol 2 puffs as needed for rescue during shortness of breath. Prednisone taper pack prescribed. Depression remains stable; continue Effexor. Continue Neurontin for chronic back pain management. Patient encouraged to do yoga for depression and back pain management.
